headline: Converting a Garage to Living Space: Key Mistakes to Avoid
articleBody:
Converting a garage into a legal bedroom, home office, or in-law suite is an effective way to gain square footage, but it comes with strict regulatory and construction hurdles. Avoiding a few frequent pitfalls will save you significant delays and unexpected costs.

Common Mistakes to Avoid:
1. Assuming your garage is already built like a house. Garages are designed to store vehicles, not keep people comfortable. Slabs often lack vapor barriers, walls may lack insulation, and ceiling joists might not be sized to carry living-space loads.
2. Starting demo before permits are approved. Treating a conversion as a cosmetic makeover can lead to stop-work orders and fines. Municipalities require building, electrical, and often mechanical permits before work begins.
3. Overlooking mandated parking requirements. Some municipalities require you to replace lost covered parking spots elsewhere on your lot before you can eliminate garage bays.
4. Underestimating the garage door opening. Framing in the old garage door opening requires a solid structural header, foundation tie-in, moisture barrier, and proper exterior finishing to avoid water intrusion.
5. Skipping required heating and egress. Habitable rooms require code-compliant heating sources and legal window openings for natural light and emergency escape.

When Professional Guidance Helps
An experienced general contractor ensures that framing, insulation, plumbing, and electrical work satisfy local building codes and pass all official city inspections.
